description:
Punch one of two. The interpreter's dispatch path answers "run this plan against these operands" through five stacked functions (src/ir_interp/backend.rs select_clause ~704, select_dispatch_body ~790, select_dispatch_match ~959; src/ir_interp/dispatch_exec.rs execute_dispatch_inputs ~74, execute_dispatch_node ~88), two of which only adapt signatures. select_dispatch_match hides DispatchOperands from its callers, so the case path (~1344) and the receive path (~1462) rebuild identical operands right after it returns, per case and per mailbox message. select_clause allocates an Absent-filled vector and clones a lane vector per required input before the first test runs. dispatch_exec.rs is 907 lines and 25 functions; twelve take six to nine parameters because runtime, module, plan, operands, state and a per-call type-test closure are threaded by hand (dispatch_region_hit takes nine). "The plan's operands beyond its inputs" is built by two functions that differ only in where a pin's value comes from: prepared_dispatch_keys (~751, entry plans: inputs[i]) and local_dispatch_pinned (~2217, match sites: env ValueIds).

Change, all shape and no representation:
- One door. Today's select_dispatch_match becomes the entry, taking &DispatchOperands; callers build operands once and reuse them for the outcome arguments. execute_dispatch_inputs and select_dispatch_body are deleted; the body-id step is one expression at the two sites that need it.
- One context. A struct owning runtime, module, types, transport, program, plan, operands and state, with the walk as methods (node, region_hit, edge_evidence, subject, bitstring, map lookup, guard). The per-call type-test closure becomes a method. Free functions with six to nine parameters become methods with one or two. The guard-helper path (eval_dispatch_guard ~471) constructs a child context for the helper plan instead of re-threading everything.
- One operand builder, taking a pin source (an input ordinal or an environment value), replacing prepared_dispatch_keys and local_dispatch_pinned.
- Borrowed arguments. The executable's decoded inputs arrive as Vec<Option<BackendBoundValue>>: None is "the ABI carries no layout for this input", Some(Absent) is "a published Nothing layout", and zero_lane_inputs_preserve_tuple_structure_without_inventing_absence pins that distinction at the decoder. The operands read through the option rather than copying past it; the required-but-missing check stays a check. Whether the two spellings of absence can collapse is a research item for this step: find every downstream reader of the difference (delivered_env, continue_backend_value, the decoder test); fold only if none reads it, otherwise leave and say so.
- Not here: the linear clause_index scan and the arm find (fz-acn.12); the state representation and prepared-key laziness (fz-21x.27, punch two).

Signal: structural, the functions that built operands twice and threaded nine parameters no longer exist, and DispatchOperands has one constructor per call site; the case, receive and entry fixture lanes on three doors; a mis-threaded state surfaces as "winning outcome lacks subject". tail_recursion interp wall clock corroborates. Ledger: adapters, closure and duplicate builder deleted; the context struct added; net negative, concept count down by five.

## UNBLOCKS

- ○ fz-21x.27 P1 Dispatch state is a dense vector with an undo journal, and prepared keys materialize on first read
- ○ fz-acn.12 P3 One body table for the six outcome-to-body lookups
- ✓ fz-acn.5 P2 Prepared dispatch keys materialize on first read
title: One door, one context, one operand builder: the interpreter's dispatch path
